items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mae had made Beezie drunk... Mae Caurance had come to Alexandria... Joe Hayman and myself moved in with Mae and Spider. Later there was an apartment on the top floor of the hotel which was the eighth floor. Mae did the cooking and we shared the expenses.

ctx.x: Jimmy opened a club in a small street called Cite Pigalle. Spider and his wife lived in this street and also Joe Hayman and wife. Bob Greir, another American Negro who had been in Paris for some time, was Jimmy's partner and the club, which I was told had never been a success for anyone that had ever tried to run it before, became a big success and meeting place for most Americans that were in Paris, and there were plenty of them. The club featured the latest jazz records and became a rendezvous place for…

One night I came home from work and Beezie was not home. We had put Joan in a private school a little outside of Paris shortly after we came from Belgium. Beezie didn't come home until about 8 o'clock that morning and when I asked her where she had been, she told me she was at Jimmy's place with Mae and Spider. I never cared much for Mae after the night I came home when she and Spider, Beezie and I were living together in the same building and Mae had made Beezie drunk by giving her cognac and wine and telling…

I didn't raise any hell because Beezie came home that late that morning but warned her not to let it happen again. Beezie and I had our ups and downs. I was very jealous and reproached her to have become too independant. We also had disputes about Joan. I thought she was too hard with the kid and she said I was too soft with her. Joan didn't get along too well with her mother.
